sections.title: Threads of Fate
sections.description: Follow the missing book, the sacrificed blade and the decisions that reached beyond a single adventure.

sections.title: The Twenty Years We Lost
sections.description: The company found its way back to a present that had carried on without it.

sections.title: The Treasury
sections.description: Weapons, books, rings and keepsakes: who carried them, what they cost and where their stories pause.

sections.title: Those We Left Behind
sections.description: From the family waiting in Oakhurst to the companions lost in Hell: people the company rescued, trusted, mourned and lost from sight.

sections.title: Voices from the Table
sections.description: Typed questions, shopping enthusiasm and campaign films from the road to the Bastion.

sections.title: The Unwritten Epilogues
sections.description: The company has reached Ashardalon. The final reckoning and the lives beyond it await their telling.

image.alt: The four companions in the campaign’s farewell film

threads.title: The book that became a brother
threads.intro: A forgotten possession gave the aboleth a body. His familiar face concealed ambitions that led back to White Plume Mountain.

nodes.title: A book goes missing
nodes.text: Grim lost and forgot a book on making flesh golems amid his dealings with the aboleth. Xanthar used its knowledge to construct the body of Brother Xanthar.

nodes.title: A place in Grim’s memories
nodes.text: Xanthar also intended to become the trusted older brother Grim remembered from childhood. The solo exposes that design; whether Grim accepted the false memories remains unknown.

nodes.title: The mountain changes hands
nodes.text: A K-vial left Xanthar convinced he was the true Keraptis. His power and constructed body spared him the zombie fate; he defeated the reigning K-clone prime and took White Plume Mountain.

nodes.title: The portal takes their belongings
nodes.text: Team Biscuit stepped through Xanthar’s portal and arrived naked. His equipment scheme returned Wave, Whelm and Frostrazor to the mountain; Ernie later recovered most of the other possessions.

threads.title: Four weapons, one sacrifice
threads.intro: The rite that broke Pengu’s hold also ended the company’s fellowship with the surviving weapons.

nodes.title: The mountain’s challenge
nodes.text: Wave, Whelm and Blackrazor entered the company’s story through White Plume Mountain. Frostrazor later joined the northern hunt for the weapons.

nodes.title: Terry bears all four
nodes.text: Pelor’s boon let Terry attune to Wave, Whelm, Frostrazor and Blackrazor together. Grim’s ingredients and candle preparations brought the working to its final stage.

nodes.title: Blackrazor is sacrificed
nodes.text: The company sacrificed Blackrazor and completed the rite. Pengu’s fighting form fell, leaving a pulsing obsidian egg as Frostblight broke apart.

nodes.title: Three voices remember
nodes.text: Wave, Whelm and Frostrazor are safely held under Xanthar’s rule in White Plume Mountain. They regard Blackrazor as their sibling, hate the Brotherhood for the sacrifice and will never forgive it.

threads.title: The village they saved
threads.intro: The rescue in Deep Horizon had consequences the Brotherhood would return too late to witness.

nodes.title: The enclave under assault
nodes.text: The company reached the desmodu amid attacks, captivity and conflict in the depths. These were people with homes and records, fighting to keep them.

nodes.title: The lava is diverted
nodes.text: The Brotherhood rerouted the lava to save the desmodu village. The immediate rescue set a slower catastrophe in motion.

nodes.title: Twenty years pass without them
nodes.text: The return from the Sleeper’s detour carried the company twenty years beyond its original present. In those missing years the diversion led to Brindinford’s volcanic destruction and the extinction of the desmodu.

nodes.title: Ants in the old streets
nodes.text: Team Biscuit returned to sunken Brindinford and fought beside Team Gravy among its ruins. The old city was now an approach to the Reality Wrinkle.

threads.title: The candle and the empty cradles
threads.intro: Pengu’s attack on magic and Ashardalon’s consumption of souls overlapped. Ending one left the other to face.

nodes.title: Shrop snuffs a candle
nodes.text: In the Nightmare Grotto, Shrop extinguished the candle that released Pengu’s spirit. The ensuing loss of magic followed the company into Icewind Dale.

nodes.title: Prayers begin to fail
nodes.text: The northern struggle exposed Pengu’s draining of magic. The company gathered the candle ingredients and four epic weapons for the ritual.

nodes.title: Magic begins to recover
nodes.text: After the completed rite and Pengu’s defeat, Eldath told the company that magic was beginning to heal. Pengu’s surviving egg still left a question behind.

nodes.title: The soul famine continues
nodes.text: The same vision named twenty years without new souls. Ashardalon was feeding upon the unborn in the Bastion; the northern victory had not ended his hunger.

threads.title: Where the two roads parted
threads.intro: The companies met in the ruins of one city. Only Team Biscuit reached Windglum.

nodes.title: Gravy comes downriver
nodes.text: Brunn, Rook, Nox and Elira survived the grotto, a falling boat and the Deliverance’s sudden rescue. The river carried them towards buried Brindinford.

nodes.title: Eight against the ants
nodes.text: Team Biscuit arrived stripped of its possessions. The two companies fought the giant ants together in the Sunken City.

nodes.title: The Wrinkle catches Gravy
nodes.text: A portal trap intended for Biscuit caught Gravy instead. Brunn, Rook, Nox and Elira were sent to Hell and remain lost there.

nodes.title: Biscuit returns to Bastion
nodes.text: The surviving route took Team Biscuit to Windglum, Findula and the search for Desayeus’s fragment. Xanthar’s equipment theft and the Wrinkle’s Hell trap remain separate events.

years.title: The Brindinford they remembered
paragraphs: Their first Brindinford was a city of streets, river traffic, a fair and a conspiracy concealed behind its Baron. They had helped free it before later adventures took them across the planes.

years.title: Home in their eighth-level lives
paragraphs: The Sleeper’s dream sent the company back into its own earlier selves. Familiar streets belonged to an earlier Brindinford, and the adventurers played once more at eighth level.
They invested with Shoomma’s smithy and the Bank of Frobozz. The return on those investments has yet to enter this account.

years.title: Their own present lay twenty years behind them
paragraphs: Finding the way out of the flashback did not restore the moment they had left. They arrived twenty years beyond their original present. Those were years the world had lived without them; the journey does not mean the companions themselves aged by twenty years.

years.title: The rescue that became a catastrophe
paragraphs: The lava diversion in Deep Horizon saved a desmodu village. During the company’s absence its consequences caused the volcanic cataclysm that destroyed Brindinford and wiped out the desmodu race.
Biscuit returned after the destruction. The later battle against the ants took place in the sunken remains of the city it remembered.

links.label: The road out of Deep Horizon

years.title: The lives that never reached birth
paragraphs: After Frostblight, the gods’ vision named twenty years without new souls being born. Ashardalon’s feeding in the Bastion was starving the world of its unborn lives.

The volcanic destruction followed the lava diversion. The soul famine followed the dragon’s hunger. Pengu’s draining of magic was another calamity, and magic could begin to recover while Ashardalon still fed.

treasury.title: Shatterspike
paragraphs: Shrop recovered Shatterspike beneath the Sunless Citadel. In Brindinford, the blade became the holy relic needed to cleanse Pelor’s occupied temple.
He sacrificed it during the company’s struggle to free the city. This earlier offering belongs to Shrop’s story; Blackrazor’s later sacrifice completed the Pengu ritual.

treasury.title: Wave
paragraphs: The trident named in Keraptis’s challenge became one of Terry’s four attuned weapons in the Pengu ritual. It survived the rite.
Revisionist: Xanthar’s scheme returned Wave to White Plume with Whelm and Frostrazor. It shares their permanent hatred of the Brotherhood for sacrificing Blackrazor.

treasury.title: Whelm
paragraphs: Whelm was gathered with the other epic weapons for Terry’s fourfold attunement. It survived the sacrifice that completed the ritual.
Revisionist: it now rests under Xanthar’s rule with Wave and Frostrazor. It remembers Blackrazor as a sibling and will never forgive the hands that offered that sibling to the rite.

treasury.title: Frostrazor
paragraphs: The northern search brought Frostrazor into the company’s struggle with Pengu and the false Keraptis. It joined Wave, Whelm and Blackrazor in Terry’s completed working.
Revisionist: Ernie did not return Frostrazor because Xanthar had taken it back to White Plume Mountain with the other survivors. Their anger endures there.

treasury.title: Blackrazor
paragraphs: The evil epic weapon was the one the company sacrificed. Terry had attuned to all four; Blackrazor’s loss completed the rite against Pengu.
Revisionist: Wave, Whelm and Frostrazor mourn it as their sibling. Blackrazor is absent from the surviving cache beneath White Plume Mountain.

treasury.title: Grim’s missing flesh-golem book
paragraphs: Grim lost and forgot a book on constructing flesh golems amid the aboleth troubles.
Revisionist: Xanthar used that knowledge to make the body he wore as Brother Xanthar. The book’s exact title and its later whereabouts remain unsettled.

treasury.title: The Candle of the Dark One
paragraphs: Grim gathered ingredients and prepared three portions of wax and three wicks. The northern working required the four epic weapons, Terry’s boon and Blackrazor’s sacrifice.
This was the ritual candle used against Pengu. The candle Shrop snuffed in the Nightmare Grotto had released the spirit earlier.

treasury.title: Pendant of the Ethereal Anchor
paragraphs: The pendant binds Thunder’s soul to Captain Timothy Pepper’s ghostly ship. In the northern vision, the Deliverance endured and searched for him.
Pepper warned that dying while wearing it would make Thunder the ship’s captive captain in his place. Neither that death nor a transfer of captaincy has been established.

treasury.title: Ernie’s four protective rings
treasury.status: Given to Team Biscuit for the crossing
paragraphs: Ernie gave each companion a Ring of Positive Energy Protection. They were meant to keep the plane’s overwhelming life from killing its visitors.
The rings and recovered possessions stayed with the company after he faded through the office door. His destination remained unknown.

treasury.title: Desayeus’s Soul Totem fragment
paragraphs: Ashardalon had entered the Bastion through another fragment of the broken Totem. The company sought the piece Desayeus still wore.
Desayeus yielded it; Thunder carried it from the prison. Eco was dead by the departure, and Findula’s farewell followed the company’s return. Desayeus remained bound.

treasury.title: The things they packed beside the weapons
paragraphs: Thunder’s dragon, unicorn and owlbear Snugglebeasts share his inventory with lockpicks and blades. Terry kept coffee, tea, sugarbombs, smith’s tools and bagpipes beside his holy weapons.
Grim’s tools, cook’s utensils and walrus recipes suggest a traveller who expected problems beyond spellcasting. The profiles keep these possessions beside the grander prizes.

leftBehind.title: Kerowyn Hucrele and the family waiting in Oakhurst
leftBehind.status: The rings and news returned to Oakhurst
paragraphs: The Hucreles were among the first people to give the expedition a purpose. Shrop and Terry helped broker the bargain with the family, whose missing children had gone beneath the Sunless Citadel.

The company returned the Hucrele rings and news of the missing adventurers. Shrop urged his companions to attend the funeral. The first journey ended with a family receiving what the dungeon had left to return.

leftBehind.title: Erky Timbers
leftBehind.status: Freed from captivity in the Citadel
paragraphs: Before the company had faced a dragon or crossed a plane, it opened a way out for Erky Timbers. The early deeds remember his release alongside Caltrop Hall, the goblin truce and the discovery of Grim.
That release is where Erky’s part in the surviving account pauses. No later journey beside the Brotherhood, death or homecoming has been established for him.

links.label: Steel, chalk and a little diplomacy

leftBehind.title: Sharwyn Hucrele and Sir Braford
leftBehind.status: Subdued beneath the Citadel
paragraphs: The missing adventurers the company confronted were already caught in Belak’s work. Grim urged that they be subdued; Shrop and Thunder helped restrain them.
Revisionist: Sharwyn and Sir Braford had been absorbed and remade as thralls of the Gulthias Tree. The later return of the rings does not supply a separate cure or final fate for each of them.

links.label: The tree and the stolen will

leftBehind.title: The twins taken into Khundrukar
leftBehind.status: Rescued; escorted to the cart
paragraphs: The twins were prisoners of the orcs when the company found them. Freeing them meant arranging a journey out of the mountain as well as opening their cell.

Terry and Thunder escorted them to the cart while Shrop and Grim remained behind. The wagon was to return in three days. Their safe passage towards Blasingdell mattered enough to divide the party before it went deeper.

links.label: Two lives worth turning back for

leftBehind.title: Arundil, and the home he could not save
leftBehind.status: The dead defender of Khundrukar
paragraphs: A ghost took an interest in Thunder in the dwarf-halls. Animated armour, a smothering rug and a kitchen table also attacked the company in the ruins of Durgeddin’s stronghold.

Revisionist: Arundil had escaped the orc assault and returned to find his people slaughtered. In grief he animated warriors and household objects to defend the fallen home. The fiend he summoned killed him. His defences survived to meet later intruders; no final rest for his spirit is recorded here.

links.label: The dead, the disguised and the furniture

leftBehind.title: Captain Aldrich
leftBehind.status: The guard captain during the occupation
paragraphs: When the company returned to the smithy, Aldrich was waiting with town guards. Turvin’s account had confirmed its suspicions about the wererats and identified Squim’s part in the pack.

Shrop befriended the guard, and Grim counselled its captain while the investigation spread across Brindinford. Aldrich belongs to the city they helped free; his later fate after their twenty-year absence has not been established.

leftBehind.title: Brindinford’s priests of Pelor
leftBehind.status: The threatened priesthood of the first city
paragraphs: Brother Calbert and High Priest Forgrim are among the faces preserved from Brindinford’s priesthood. The Baron’s decrees outlawed the priests, and the temple beneath the golden dome became a battlefield.

The company fought the infernal occupation and cleansed the temple with Shatterspike as its holy relic. Terry committed himself to Pelor during these adventures. The priests’ individual lives after the company left remain outside the account.

leftBehind.title: Baron Euphemes
leftBehind.status: Freed from Ghaerleth Axom’s control
paragraphs: The ruler behind Brindinford’s decrees was himself a captive. In the manor, the company reached the mind flayer Ghaerleth Axom, whose control had made the Baron part of the town’s occupation.

Terry’s Daylight helped save Euphemes, and the mind flayer fell. The Baron lifted martial law; the fair resumed with food, wine and dancing. His freedom belongs to that earlier victory, before the ruined city the company would one day return to.

leftBehind.title: Shoomma, Horken and the smithy
leftBehind.status: Investments left in an earlier Brindinford
paragraphs: The smithy was a place to rest during the city’s first crisis. In the Sleeper’s detour the company returned to an earlier Brindinford and entrusted investments to Shoomma’s smithy, associated with Horken, as well as the Bank of Frobozz.

They left money and equipment in a city whose future they had already lived through once. Their eventual return overshot their own present by twenty years. The smithy’s later fate, the people’s survival and any repayment remain untold.

leftBehind.title: Saithnar
leftBehind.status: Last met in the Great Barrows
paragraphs: Dyson’s warnings did not stop the company from speaking with the ancient warlord. Grim offered gems in respect, and Thunder alone managed to strike Saithnar when he challenged them.

Saithnar gave them a map and told them of Dydd, Ashardalon and Gulthias Sengir. His spectacles helped Thunder translate the dragon-lore margins for Grim and Terry. The company travelled on towards Nightfang with knowledge gained from a dead man it had chosen to hear.

leftBehind.title: Pelor’s headless Horseman
leftBehind.status: The paladin at Red Horse Hill
paragraphs: The company cleaned his abandoned shrine, refilled its basins and questioned the dead paladin. His account named Dyson as his killer and described his own work as containing the villagers and protecting the elves.

Terry’s communion strengthened his commitment to Pelor. The Horseman’s armour and shield were later returned to the temple in Brindinford. He was a different figure from Saithnar, with a different duty; the return of his equipment does not establish that his vigil ended.

leftBehind.title: The people inside Ossington’s stones
leftBehind.status: The village turned on its would-be rescuers
paragraphs: Team Biscuit arrived with carts of food and seed for hungry Ossington. The village later attacked the company, and Tully fell in the fighting.

Revisionist: Dyson’s recovered note identified Tully as his cat familiar, transformed into a convincing human. That discovery exposed one false identity among the supposed retired adventurers. It does not make every villager the same experiment, or turn the ending into a successful rescue of the whole village.

leftBehind.title: The druids’ missing son
leftBehind.status: Found dead in the Grugach settlement
paragraphs: In the Grugach settlement the company found the missing druid’s son dead. Thunder’s work with a locked door helped establish the fate the party had been sent to discover.

They carried the report back to Brindinford and secured the Druids of Dydd’s help for Ossington’s land and food supply. The return brought news to those waiting for him, rather than the missing man himself.

links.label: The discovery and the older history

leftBehind.title: Eudostis
leftBehind.status: Homecoming unrecorded
paragraphs: Before the company learned of the Time Stone, Grim recognised a familiar gnome’s likeness on a sarcophagus in Nightfang’s Hall of Tombs. He later identified Eudostis Braidedbeard as his great-grandfather; the carved honour concealed a relative still living under another shape.
He stole the Time Stone hoping to free the Sleeper and inadvertently opened the lock upon Crimson Crazuk. Lydzin later wished him into a parrot, and captivity damaged his mind.
The Sleeper partially repaired him and recommended sending him home. His safe arrival remains a thread Grim can still ask about.

links.label: The likeness in the Hall of Tombs
The Sleeper and the Time Stone

leftBehind.title: The captives beneath the surface
leftBehind.status: Their individual homecomings remain unrecorded
paragraphs: Helkitrin’s account overturned an explanation the company had accepted: people believed burned with Blasingdell had instead been taken below by the Stolen Sons. Other captives came from Ossington, the wild elves, Hunters Ports and Brindinford.

His records traced the exchange of slaves for refined metal and the prisoners’ passage towards beholders at an old drow temple. The company exposed that route. The surviving account does not name every captive or establish who eventually reached home.

links.label: The familiar towns on the same route

leftBehind.title: The desmodu
leftBehind.status: A people lost during the missing twenty years
paragraphs: In Deep Horizon the company met defenders, captives and keepers of records. The Brotherhood’s lava diversion saved their village.
The delayed consequences of that diversion brought Brindinford’s volcanic destruction and the extinction of the desmodu during the company’s absence. No later homecoming to the enclave awaited them.

links.label: What happened while they were gone

leftBehind.title: Thunder’s Brindinford guildmates
leftBehind.status: The Rigus meeting ended in slaughter
paragraphs: Thunder arranged to meet the last surviving members of his Brindinford guild in Rigus. The meeting became a slaughter, and he emerged with blood-spattered notes.

Those pages described earlier losses to Rigus’s local guild, members forced into mercenary bands and a Guildmaster in hiding. The road had taken the guild far from Brindinford. The recovered account does not name the meeting’s attackers or establish the Guildmaster’s eventual fate.

links.label: The meeting and the bloodied notes

leftBehind.title: Team Gravy
leftBehind.status: Still lost in Hell
paragraphs: Brunn, Rook, Nox and Elira fought beside Team Biscuit against the ants in sunken Brindinford. The trap in the Reality Wrinkle had been set for Biscuit; Gravy went through it instead.
Their last established destination is Hell. No rescue, death or return has been written for them.

leftBehind.title: Findula
leftBehind.status: The alliance ended
paragraphs: The company helped free the lillend, and she repaid it by finding Eco and the route to Desayeus. Eco was her sister.
After Eco’s death, Findula left her note, accepted her part in the cost and declared the debt settled. She neither expected nor wished to speak with the company again.

leftBehind.title: Eco
leftBehind.status: Died before the company left the prison
paragraphs: The solar guarded Desayeus with Bramam. Her body was the doorway the company needed.
By the time Thunder carried out the fragment, Eco was dead. Findula’s letter placed that loss beside the company’s need to stop Ashardalon.

links.label: The guardian who was the door

leftBehind.title: Brother Ernie
leftBehind.status: Departed; destination unknown
paragraphs: Believed lost in the irionite-bomb explosion, Ernie returned with most of the company’s belongings. His smile, gestures and devoted interpretive dance did the work of an explanation.
He gave four protective rings, embraced the companions and faded into warm motes beyond the door. His departure does not establish his death.

leftBehind.title: Captain Timothy Pepper
leftBehind.status: Captaincy and bargain unresolved
paragraphs: Pepper’s Deliverance caught the falling boat above Brindinford Falls and carried Thunder’s soul-bond through the company’s later dream.
His warning remains: if Thunder dies wearing the pendant, Thunder takes the captive captain’s place. Pepper’s freedom has not been established.

links.label: The ship beside the falling boat

quotes.speaker: grim
quotes.title: The three Ernie could not bring back
quotes.quote: Brother Ernie, if I understand you correctly, my relative had possession of the three special weapons and you were not able to get them away from him?
quotes.context: At the reunion, Grim questioned Ernie about the missing weapons. His question preserves the company’s suspicion at that moment. Revisionist: their destination was White Plume Mountain under Xanthar’s rule.

quotes.speaker: shrop
quotes.title: Asking leave to enter
quotes.quote: We are with Eco. She said if you command her, she will obey. Does Eco have your leave to open the way to Desayus?
quotes.context: Shrop’s typed appeal sought Pelor’s permission to pass Eco and speak with the prisoner. The original spelling is retained.

quotes.speaker: thunder
quotes.title: The blood he carried
quotes.quote: in the name of Dydd, whose blood is my blood, who slew your heart feel again the pain of your heart's demise
quotes.context: Thunder typed the invocation in Desayeus’s prison. It records his claim to Dydd’s bloodline; the final confrontation with Ashardalon still awaits its account.

quotes.speaker: grim
quotes.title: A brief statement of financial intent
quotes.quote: I am here to spend all my money on frivolities!
quotes.context: Grim’s contribution to the shopping chat needs little explanation. No expenditure total is implied.

intro: The account reaches the company inside the Bastion, with Ashardalon and Ammet still ahead. The GM’s account of the final confrontation will fill these pages. No victory, death, restored soul cycle or homecoming is assumed.

company.title: Ashardalon and Ammet
company.text: The dragon survives through the demon within his ruined heart. What becomes of each must be told separately.

company.title: The unborn souls
company.text: Stopping the dragon’s feeding and establishing the fate of the souls are questions the final account must answer.

company.title: The road home
company.text: Who leaves the Bastion, where they go and what they return to remain open.

characters.text: Shrop has reached the Bastion fighting without sight. Caroleena’s fate, his conscription and the soldier’s final choice still leave room for his own ending.
Ashardalon awaits the scholar who studied him. The surrendered memories, the family diamond, his great spellbook and Eudostis’s homecoming remain threads beyond the dragon.
The priest completed the Pengu rite. His altered behaviour remains a separate question, as do his future with Pelor, Zandikar and the companions.
Dydd’s descendant has spoken the invocation. His curse, his mother’s reunion and the Deliverance’s captaincy await answers beyond the recorded journey.
The Wrinkle sent Nox to Hell with the other three. Her next bargain, rescue or return has not been established.
Brunn’s road ends here beside his companions in Hell. His survival beyond that last known destination remains unwritten.
Rook survived the falling boat and fought in the buried city before the Hell trap caught Gravy. No flight home has yet been recorded.
Elira went through the trap with Team Gravy. Her fate and any return from Hell remain open.

looseEnds.title: The mountain still holds three weapons
looseEnds.text: Wave, Whelm and Frostrazor remain with Xanthar and will never forgive the Brotherhood. A victory at the Bastion would not by itself settle that grievance.

looseEnds.title: The egg after Frostblight
looseEnds.text: Pengu’s fighting form fell, but the obsidian egg still pulsed and drew warmth. Its later fate has not been established.

looseEnds.title: The investments left in an earlier Brindinford
looseEnds.text: The smithy and Bank of Frobozz held investments. No balance, payout or recovery has been established after the return.

looseEnds.title: Friends beyond the last door
looseEnds.text: Findula ended the alliance, Ernie departed and Team Gravy remained in Hell. Each has a different last known ending.

farewellEras.title: Oakhurst and the Sunless Citadel
farewellEras.intro: A bargain with a waiting family, a prisoner freed and adventurers found beneath the roots.

farewellEras.title: Blasingdell and the Forge of Fury
farewellEras.intro: The living needed a way out of Khundrukar. The dead had left their defences running.

farewellEras.title: The first Brindinford
farewellEras.intro: The city had guards, priests, a smithy and people who could celebrate when the fighting ended.

farewellEras.title: Ossington and the standing stones
farewellEras.intro: The company brought food to the village and left with a very different account of its protectors.

farewellEras.title: A family face at Nightfang Spire
farewellEras.intro: Grim found his ancestor’s likeness among the honoured dead. The story behind it was still moving.

farewellEras.title: The people beneath the surface
farewellEras.intro: Missing townsfolk had been taken into the slave trade. The desmodu faced an assault upon their home.

farewellEras.title: Rigus and the later roads
farewellEras.intro: Guildmates, shipmates and companions crossed the planar roads. Some parted by choice; others were taken.
